A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Renumbered figures, revised notation, and relocated proofs can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations in the two-state/two-action, Beach Bar, and Night Clubs environments, including imitation errors, rewards, exploitability, and five-run summaries in Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation results and their appendix analyses, with additional main-text displays of selected convergence curves.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the best-response target from policies through pi^k to policies through pi^(k−1), removing a circular reference in the written update. This aligns the pseudocode with v1's existing explanation; the architectures, imitation objectives, and overall learning framework remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three synthetic environments and common-noise parameter grids. The added classification of noise mechanisms in Section 4.3 describes existing scenarios rather than expanding tested coverage.

E2.justification: Population-unaware Vanilla remains the comparator to population-aware Adaptive, with Expert retained as the reference in policy comparisons. No evaluated baseline is added or removed; changes to related-work citations do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Appendix B's Algorithm 4 now explicitly computes BC and ADV discrepancies at time zero; v1 initialized them to zero and updated only later times. This corrects the stated proxy-evaluation procedure. Parameter grids and training settings remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The parameter-sensitivity grids, policy-response case studies, and training/convergence analyses are retained. v2 Figures 4 and 8 redisplay selected configurations already analyzed in v1 Figures 15 and 19; they introduce no new ablation or analytical question.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent full-pipeline runs, averages, standard deviations, and shaded plots. v2 consolidates the run-count description into Section 4.3. No new seed information, significance testing, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark values, standard-deviation heatmaps, and policy-comparison results are preserved. The mean convergence curves in new v2 Figures 4 and 8 match the corresponding v1 appendix curves, but their shaded fictitious-play ranges differ slightly. This is a limited change to displayed uncertainty values, without evidence of improved performance.

T1.justification: Assumption 2.4 changes from bounding rewards along the expert population flow to bounding them along flows induced by every policy. Appendix A also repairs the missing absolute values in Lemma A.3's occupancy-difference bound. The theorem bounds remain unchanged, and their short proofs are relocated rather than newly supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: imitation learning with common noise, BC/ADV guarantees, generalized fictitious play with policy distillation, and the importance of population awareness.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly interprets success across the three noise mechanisms as demonstrating superiority regardless of the common-noise manifestation. Additional convergence commentary interprets existing training curves. This expands the discussion of applicability without adding limitations or evidence covering arbitrary noise forms.

D1.justification: Tables 1–3 and Appendices C–E retain the same architectures, optimizers, learning rates, training budgets, sample counts, discretization, and kernel bandwidth. No additional hardware, runtime, or code/data-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Carmona, Delarue, and Lacker (2016) for common-noise theory and replaces Yang et al. (2018) with Elie et al. (2020) in its attribution of early reinforcement learning for MFGs. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, revises common-noise notation, consolidates repeated experimental prose, and moves the existing theorem proofs into Appendix A.2. The main section sequence and overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds compact main-text convergence Figures 4 and 8 using selected configurations from the retained appendix plots. Other changes concern figure renumbering, caption corrections, float placement, and page reflow; the existing tables and principal result displays retain their structure.

improvement.justification: The stronger reward-boundedness assumption better matches the proofs, Lemma A.3's missing absolute values are repaired, and Algorithm 4 now includes initial-time errors. These corrections and clearer proof organization provide a limited improvement in correctness and readability. Experimental coverage and central results remain unchanged, while the new claim of superiority regardless of noise form exceeds what three synthetic examples establish.
